Standard: Landing lights have a minimum intensity value of 300,000 cd with a minimum beam spread of 8 degrees in the vertical plane and 14 degrees total in the horizontal plane measured from the centerline of the air vehicle. The beam spread is defined as the beam angle where the intensity drops to 10% of the maximum intensity. Landing lights are free of dangerous glare or halation to the pilots. The chromaticity for landing lights will be Aviation White. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Landing light(s) coverage, aimability, and intensity are verified by geometric and photometric analysis. Demonstration.
  (1) Conduct a demonstration on the air vehicle to verify the landing light(s) aimability and that the design of the landing light(s) minimizes glare to the pilots. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Conduct component-level testing of the landing light test article to measure chromaticity, beam spread, and intensity.
    (2) Ground test: Perform testing on the air vehicle to measure the light intensity at required beam spread angles as measured from the air vehicle centerline.
